terms.comment: Ancient verb; Lewis & Short gives it no classical perfect, and extulī is the perfect of efferō. This entry does not supply a speculative full set of principal parts.
Use it for a past-tense “we raised the walls.”

phrases.latin: Parietēs altius exstrūximus et novum tēctum imposuimus.
phrases.english: We built the walls up higher and put on the new roof.

sources: Lewis & Short: extollo · Lewis & Short: exstruo · Lewis & Short: effero
The example sentence marked “composed” is ours.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 165, each phrase checked against the searchable text of the book.
